hints.title: Subproblem Identification
hints.text: For each element, you must decide whether to apply no operation, operation 1, operation 2, or both operations.

hints.title: Order of Combined Operations
hints.text: When both operations are applied, dividing then subtracting can produce a different result than subtracting then dividing.

hints.title: State Formulation
hints.text: Define state (index, remaining op1, remaining op2) and take the minimum across all valid choices for the current index.

hints.title: Reference Implementation

complexity.notes: Dynamic programming evaluates 5 choices per element: none, op1, op2, op1 then op2, or op2 then op1.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy choices fail because the optimal ordering of operations depends on specific numeric thresholds.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Designs state transitions covering all five possible operation applications per index.
